eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Hong Kong’s June 15 maximum temperature centers on 28–30 °C**, with 29 °C holding the highest implied probability (41.5 %) followed by 28 °C (31 %) and 30 °C (18.5 %). These probabilities reflect the current consensus from numerical weather prediction models and the Hong Kong Observatory’s guidance for mid-June conditions under an above-normal seasonal temperature outlook.

Hong Kong’s subtropical climate in June features warm, moist southwesterly flow, high humidity (often >80 %), and frequent convective showers or thunderstorms that limit extreme daytime heating. Model consensus for June 15 points to a maximum near 28–30 °C (roughly 82–86 °F), consistent with climatological daily highs of 29–31 °C and the influence of possible thundershowers that can cap temperatures through cloud cover and evaporative cooling. Lower outcomes (27 °C or below) carry reduced weight because recent model runs show limited cooling, while probabilities above 31 °C remain low given the moderating effects of moisture and precipitation.

The Hong Kong Observatory’s seasonal forecast for June–August 2026, issued in late May, highlights above-normal temperatures driven by long-term warming trends and ENSO-neutral conditions, supporting the market’s concentration around the upper end of typical June values. Short-term updates on June 14 indicate persistent humid conditions with thunder activity, reinforcing the 28–30 °C cluster as the most likely range ahead of final observations on the 15th.

With resolution occurring within hours, the market largely mirrors the current short-range forecast consensus rather than longer-term seasonal signals.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for the highest temperature in Panama City, Panama, on June 15 centers on the narrow 30–31°C range because mid-June wet-season conditions produce highly variable daily maxima driven by the timing and intensity of afternoon convection.**

In Panama’s rainy season (May–December), the Intertropical Convergence Zone fuels widespread moisture and instability, so mornings often start with partial cloud cover that can either burn off to allow stronger solar heating or persist and trigger thunderstorms by early afternoon. These storms reduce insolation and bring evaporative cooling, frequently capping the day’s peak 1–2°C lower than a clear-sky scenario would permit. Historical INAMEH records show June maxima clustering tightly between 29–32°C, with 30°C and 31°C occurring at roughly comparable frequencies depending on exactly when convective cells develop over the isthmus.

Current model guidance and climatological baselines place the most probable outcome near the long-term mean of ~30–31°C, but small shifts in steering flow, moisture convergence, or the precise hour of storm initiation can easily swing the recorded high by a single degree. With no large-scale anomalies such as an unusually strong or suppressed monsoon trough present, the market’s near-even split between 30°C (33.5%) and 31°C (34.0%) reflects this inherent short-term uncertainty in tropical convective timing rather than any decisive recent weather event. Updated National Meteorological Service guidance and high-resolution model runs on June 15 morning will provide the final data traders need to refine positions before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 16 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader sentiment centers on the narrow gap between 34°C and 35°C outcomes because short-range forecast guidance for June 16 places Karachi’s daily maximum squarely in that range amid typical pre-monsoon conditions.** Coastal location near the Arabian Sea supplies moderating maritime air and afternoon sea breezes that cap peaks, while high humidity and light winds can allow slight warming if subsidence or clearer skies develop. Recent model runs and Pakistan Meteorological Department guidance show highs near 32–34°C (roughly 90–93°F), consistent with June climatology where the most probable daily maxima cluster between 34–36°C. Minor differences in cloud cover, wind direction, or timing of any weak trough will determine whether the peak reaches 35°C or stays at 34°C; updated model runs and official briefings in the next 24–48 hours are the key variables traders are watching.
